evidence_spans: Here, the molten salt corrosion behavior of AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) was evaluated in molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl 2 salt at 450 °C and 650 °C in comparison to conventional duplex stainless steel 2205 (DS2205).
The EHEA showed a significantly lower corrosion rate of ~1 mm/year at 450 °C compared to ~8 mm/year for DS2205.
Similarly, EHEA showed a lower corrosion rate of ~9 mm/year at 650 °C compared to ~20 mm/year for DS2205.

cross_paper_synthesis.consensus: Both sources confirm a potential difference of approximately 50 mV is associated with AlCoCrFeNi 2.1. One source specifies this as a contrast between phases, while the other cites an average value relative to DS2205. Both agree the numerical values are ~50 mV for AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 and ~-65 mV for DS2205.
cross_paper_synthesis.different_approaches: The first approach focuses on the spatial distribution of potential, characterizing the 50 mV value as a 'contrast difference between phases' within the microstructure, likely referring to micro-galvanic coupling [PMC9955357::reader_question::d08be92ad37161fc::answer::952d9136dbde8a53]. The second approach focuses on bulk comparison and sign convention, defining the value as an 'overall relative work function potential' average and explicitly noting the lack of a stated correlation between the potential sign and nobility [PMC9955357::reader_question::69ad72d854fe43ca::answer::dec1b4d1d9edef39].
cross_paper_synthesis.condition_dependencies: The characterization of the 50 mV as a phase contrast implies a measurement taken at room temperature on a dual-phase surface, likely using Scanning Kelvin Probe (SKP), while the average comparison to DS2205 is reported under high-temperature corrosion conditions (450 °C in molten salt), though the text does not explicitly link the sign convention to these different regimes.
cross_paper_synthesis.contradictions: No direct contradictions exist; however, there is a lack of explicit definition regarding whether the 'contrast' and the 'average relative potential' refer to the exact same metric or if one is a subset of the other. The primary gap is the absence of a definitive sign convention in the text to determine if positive potential (50 mV) directly implies higher nobility compared to the negative value (-65 mV) [PMC9955357::reader_question::69ad72d854fe43ca::answer::dec1b4d1d9edef39].
cross_paper_synthesis.evidence_strength: Cited values for the 50 mV and -65 mV are explicitly stated in the source text, but the interpretation of these values regarding spatial uniformity and electrochemical nobility is marked as 'unspecified' or 'not specified in evidence'.
cross_paper_synthesis.unresolved_gap: It is unresolved whether the ~50 mV value is a uniform contrast across the entire microstructure or merely an average of specific regions [PMC9955357::reader_question::d08be92ad37161fc::answer::952d9136dbde8a53], and the specific sign convention used to correlate these work function potentials to the nobility of the alloys is not defined [PMC9955357::reader_question::69ad72d854fe43ca::answer::dec1b4d1d9edef39].
cross_paper_synthesis.candidate_hypothesis: The ~50 mV represents the maximum potential difference driving micro-galvanic corrosion between phases in AlCoCrFeNi 2.1, while the -65 mV value for DS2205 represents a bulk average; the sign convention likely follows standard SKP measurements where more positive potentials indicate higher nobility, but this convention is not explicitly stated in the provided text.
cross_paper_synthesis.discriminating_experiment: Perform spatially resolved Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy (KPFM) at room temperature to map the full potential distribution of AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 to distinguish between uniform phase contrast and localized averages, and simultaneously measure open-circuit potentials (OCP) in the molten salt environment to empirically correlate the sign of the work function with corrosion rates (nobility).
